summary: The study investigates the plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Ta2O5 using pentakis(dimethylamino)tantalum (PDMA T) as the tantalum precursor and remote O2 plasma as the oxidant. The process was carried out at temperatures ranging from 100 to 225 °C. The films were found to be stoichiometric (Ta:O = 2:5) with no nitrogen incorporation and low carbon content. The mass density of the films was close to the bulk Ta2O5 density, and the films were amorphous. The growth rate varied between 0.8 Å/cycle at 225 °C and 0.87 Å/cycle at 100 °C. The reaction mechanisms during the plasma step were studied using quadrupole mass spectrometry and optical emission spectroscopy, revealing combustion-like processes where alkylamide ligands were oxidized by O radicals generated in the plasma.
evidence: Tantalum oxide (Ta2O5) films were synthesized by plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition from pentakis(dimethylamino)tantalum (PDMA T) precursor and remote O2 plasma as oxidation source. Film growth was monitored in situ by spectroscopic ellipsometry, and film properties were investigated for deposition temperatures between 100 and 225 °C. The deposited films were found to be stoichiometric (Ta:O=2:5). The mass density of the films, ranging from 7.8 g cm−3 at 100 °C to 8.1 g cm−3 at 225 °C, was found to be close to the bulk Ta2O5 density. X-ray diffraction revealed that all films were amorphous, independent of deposition temperature. The reaction mechanisms, in particular, during the plasma step, were investigated by using quadrupole mass spectrometry and optical emission spectroscopy. During the plasma step, combustion products such as CO, CO2, and H2O were detected. This indicates that combustion-like processes occur, in which the alkylamide N(CH3)2 ligands are oxidized by the O radicals generated in the plasma.
